## US moves diplomats out of region, Trump threatens new Iran operation
The US is moving some diplomats and families out of Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar and Jordan, CNN reported. Axios said intelligence on alleged Iranian assassination plots helped prompt the staffing reductions.
The United States could launch another military operation against Iran unless Tehran reaches an agreement with Washington, President Donald Trump said Friday at a rally in Florida.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said oil exports from the Persian Gulf had surpassed pre-war levels despite Iran’s attempts to disrupt energy shipments.
Masoud Pezeshkian is expected at the eighth Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow on October 27. Abbas Araghchi said Pezeshkian would travel to Moscow and meet Vladimir Putin next week.
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said most technical preparations to verify Iran’s nuclear activities were complete. He said the agency was ready and a lasting solution required a diplomatic agreement.

## Kayhan editor says Iran will reclaim Bahrain
Bahrain belongs to Iran and will be taken back when the time comes, Hossein Shariatmadari, editor-in-chief of the hardline Kayhan newspaper, said, according to Eslahat News.
“Bahrain belongs to us. When the time comes, we will take it back,” Shariatmadari said.

## Iranian hardliners urge withdrawal from nuclear non-proliferation treaty
An Iranian hardline political group has called on parliament and the Supreme National Security Council to begin the process of withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), arguing that the agreement has failed to protect Iran's nuclear facilities and national security.
The Paydari Front, a hardline faction aligned with the Islamic Republic's conservative establishment, accused the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of facilitating attacks on Iran rather than protecting its peaceful nuclear activities, according to a statement published by Didban Iran.
The group said that ending Iran's NPT membership would reduce international oversight, strengthen deterrence and protect nuclear facilities and scientists, despite the possibility of additional Western sanctions.
It urged authorities to accelerate withdrawal procedures, end cooperation beyond treaty obligations and revise Iran's military and defense doctrine.

## Iran's state media reports death of Basij militia member
A member of Iran’s Basij paramilitary force has died after spending around nine months in a coma following injuries sustained during nationwide anti-government protests in January 2026, Iranian state television reported.
The Basij force has been used to suppress anti-government protests in Iran.
Mohammadreza Talebi was injured on January 9 in Tehran’s District 7, according to the state broadcaster.

## Iran judiciary chief says Israel seeks Iran’s destruction
Israel seeks to destroy Iran rather than merely divide the country, and the Islamic Republic views Israel’s existence as a danger to humanity, Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei said.
“We must not forget that our current war with the enemy is an existential war,” Ejei said on Saturday.

## Iran’s Guards say they struck Kurdish PJAK group’s training site
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards attacked a site used by the Kurdish armed group PJAK for meetings and training, Mehr news agency reported Saturday.
Mehr described the attack as a preemptive operation, saying intelligence monitoring indicated that PJAK members were preparing an operation under orders from their commanders. It said the targeted positions were destroyed.
The report gave no location or casualty figures.

## Trump suggests turning US warships toward Cuba after Iran
US President Donald Trump suggested sending a US warship close to Cuba’s coast after the Iran war, reviving the prospect of military intervention during a campaign rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on Friday.
Trump said ships returning from the Middle East could stop near the island, predicting that its leaders would surrender before Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived to negotiate.
“We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal,” Trump said.
Shortly afterward, Rubio urged people seeking political change in Cuba to work with the CIA, writing on social media that “now is the time."

The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen’s Houthis toward Riyadh.

## Iran military chief says US warships will not be allowed into Persian Gulf
Iran will not allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf “under any circumstances,” Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ali Abdollahi said on Saturday, according to the IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency.
“We will not, under any circumstances or at any time, allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf,” Abdollahi said.
He claimed Iran’s armed forces had rendered the US Navy ineffective and said American forces were no longer able to approach waters around the Persian Gulf or Iran’s territorial waters.
“The US president can only dream of their military and army entering the Persian Gulf again,” Abdollahi said, Tasnim reported.
Oct 24, 2026, 04:41 GMT+1
## UK foreign secretary says Iran war has gone on ‘too long’
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Friday that the Iran war and Tehran’s attacks on shipping were driving up energy and food bills and inflation in Britain, calling for diplomacy to bring the conflict to a lasting end.
“The Iran war and Iran’s attacks on shipping are raising energy bills, raising food bills, raising inflation,” Miliband told reporters in Istanbul, where he was attending talks with European and regional counterparts.
“Diplomacy, dialogue and de-escalation has to be the answer to this conflict,” he said.
“Frankly, this conflict has gone on too long. The British people have suffered too much from it, and we cannot afford months more of it,” Miliband added. The Istanbul meeting brought together foreign ministers from Britain, France, Germany and Italy with counterparts from Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt.
